title: Reuters Interview: More Hikes Likely, but No Urgency to Act in October
summary: In an exclusive Reuters interview on the day of a hotter-than-expected September CPI (press coverage only), Daly says the Fed is 'more likely than not' to need additional rate increases, but that the timing is still being deliberated and there is no urgency to act at the October meeting with limited information. The CPI print shows the risk to inflation remains elevated and has gone up, yet she frames it as driven by gasoline with sticky but not re-accelerating underlying inflation, and argues that 'risks are not realities' and reacting on risk when there is time to decide well would be imprudent. A stable labor market gives the Fed room to focus on price stability. Versus the Oct. 6 Axios interview, where further hikes hinged on whether the shocks proved temporary, she now states more tightening as the more likely outcome, while explicitly arguing against an October move.

key_quotes.quote: We are more likely than not to need additional adjustments, but the timing of those adjustments to me is something we're still deliberating
key_quotes.context: Further hikes as the more likely path; timing open.

key_quotes.quote: The risk to inflation has gone up more, but risks are not realities, and reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent.
key_quotes.context: Inflation risk up after CPI, but no case for urgency in October.

key_quotes.quote: Why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency?
